rationale: Slot in the Manichaean ecclesiastical ladder (teachers > X > presbyters) corresponds to ἐπίσκοποι. Etymology unclear — possibly native Coptic plural from a root for 'oversight,' or a borrowing not yet identified. Translation by hierarchical position pending etymological clarity.

In the phrase ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲧⲡⲓⲧⲟⲩ ('into the X of...'), context demands a noun signifying assent or commitment. Possibly Greek πειθώ 'persuasion' or πίστις 'trust' through Lyc. phonological adaptation. Tentative.
Coptic causative of ⲥⲧⲟ 'turn' with directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'away.' Used in line 8 of one who 'turns aside' from the ordination — ecclesiastical apostasy. Preserves spatial semantics.
Greek loanword from αἰτητής/αἰτηταί 'askers, suppliants.' Used here for those who petition/request from before God; appropriate to context of intercessory or eschatological appeal.
Lyc. form, possibly reduplicated of ⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'join, shut, embrace.' Reflexive imperative with ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'into' = 'gather/bind yourselves into.' Used paraenetically of communal cohesion.
